title: Typed Action Streamlet SDK — PRD sketch
body:
Summary:
This PRD sketch proposes a compact, typed streaming surface ("Streamlet") for the Hosted API focused on: low-latency incremental output, explicit typed action frames for tool-calling, and an ergonomics-focused SDK that makes progressive results natural for client apps. The Streamlet is intended to sit alongside our existing streaming envelope but provide a smaller, strongly-typed subset optimized for mobile and microservice integrations where bandwidth and parseability matter.

Problem statement / motivation:
- Current streaming surfaces prioritize maximal flexibility (free-form tokens + incremental delta updates). That is powerful but produces brittle parsing for toolchains and fragile UX on slow networks.
- Many partner integrations want 1) predictable partial JSON structures, 2) deterministic action boundaries for tool calls, and 3) minimal framing overhead for low-power clients.
- SDK teams continue to implement client-side heuristics to stitch partial responses; this results in duplicated, buggy logic across languages.

Goals / non-goals:
Goals:
- Provide a typed incremental envelope that guarantees each emitted frame is parseable (valid JSON snippet or typed action token).
- Make tool-calling explicit: action frames include typed metadata (action-type, args-schema-version, call-id) for safe client invocation and replay.
- Enable resumability from a frame checkpoint (lightweight sequence checkpoint).
- Offer an SDK contract across JS/Python/Go that abstracts reconnection, resume, and typed deserialization.
- Keep latency SLOs unchanged or improved vs current streaming.
Non-goals:
- This is not a replacement for the full streaming API; complex, unbounded token streaming (e.g., free-form long-form generation) stays on the existing surface.

Success metrics:
- Developer adoption: 30% of new streaming-integrations prefer Streamlet surface within 3 months of GA.
- Fewer client bugs: 50% reduction in SDK-driven partial-parse support tickets in quarter following rollout.
- Latency: 90th percentile latency for first structured frame <= current streaming latency + 15ms.
- Bandwidth: <10% extra overhead vs raw token stream for equivalent content payloads.

Design overview (high level):
- Streamlet frames are self-contained small JSON objects; there are two primary frame kinds: "progress" frames and "action" frames.
- Progress frames: typed partial payloads (summary fragments, structured objects, incremental arrays) that can be merged deterministically by the SDK.
- Action frames: explicit action-call instructions (tool call request, tool result) with typed schemas for args and results.
- Checkpoints: periodic compact checkpoint frames with sequence_id + serialized minimal resume-token (opaque to clients but stable across model variants).

Frame examples (sketch):
- Progress frame (single-line streaming item):
  {"kind":"progress","seq":1234,"payload":{"section":"summary","part_index":0,"text":"We recommend moving the compute to the edge..."}}
- Action-call request frame:
  {"kind":"action","seq":1235,"action":{"id":"call-42","type":"search","schema_version":"v2","args":{"q":"latency budgeting"}},"meta":{"timeout_ms":2000}}
- Action-result frame (tool returns and model synthesizes final block):
  {"kind":"action_result","seq":1236,"action_id":"call-42","status":"ok","result":{"hits":12,"top_1":{"title":"Latency patterns","url":"https://..."}}}

API surface and ergonomics (client-centric):
- Low-friction connectors: SDK exposes a StreamletClient with methods: openStream(params), on('progress', cb), on('action', cb), resume(stream_id, resume_token).
- Default behavior: SDK buffers small progress frames (<128 bytes) and emits a merged "stable_progress" event every 200ms to reduce chattiness for apps that don't need micro updates.
- For tool-calling, SDK returns a typed action handle to app code that provides accept()/reject()/decorate() helpers and ensures idempotency across retries.
- Offline-friendly mode: SDK can optionally persist last checkpoint to client storage and attempt transparent resume after reconnect.

Server-side behaviors / runtime implications:
- Kernel selection: frames are assembled at the call-edge; runtime must ensure action frames are emitted atomically (no mid-action token interleaving).
- Batching: Streamlet prioritizes small atomic frames; server should group adjacent progress fragments for throughput efficiency but not delay action frames.
- Fallbacks: If model cannot produce typed content, server can emit a legacy token stream fallback flagged with {"kind":"compat_fallback"}. SDKs detect and surface telemetry.

Structured schemas and versioning:
- Schemas are small JSON-Schema-ish contracts referenced by schema_version strings (e.g. "result:search:v2"). The PRD proposes a lightweight registry: schema ids + human-readable description embedded in a single-shot metadata frame at stream start.
- Backwards compatibility: clients MUST ignore unknown fields; schema_version upgrades are opt-in at the client API.

Telemetry / Observability requirements:
- Emit per-frame timing: server->client latency, action-roundtrip time, resume success/failure. SDK will surface these as events and include opt-in sampling hooks for Console traces.
- Error taxonomy: malformed-frame, schema-mismatch, action-timeout, resume-failed. Server increments appropriate counters and attaches trace_id to action frames.

SDK contract details (sketch):
- Language SDKs (JS/Py/Go) provide: StreamletClient, ActionHandle, CheckpointStore interface (pluggable), and an SDK adapter for hosted-api auth + reconnect policy.
- Default reconnect policy: exponential backoff with jitter; resume attempts limited to 3 before surfacing failure to app.
- Security: action frames containing sensitive args should be flagged with "sensitive":true; SDK must avoid persisting those in local checkpoint stores.

Migration and compatibility story:
- Coexistence: Existing streaming endpoints keep current behavior. New endpoint param (?surface=streamlet) toggles typed frame emission.
- Gradual rollout: beta customers receive both legacy and streamlet concurrently via a header; clients can opt-in.

Experiment plan / playbook (MVP):
- Phase 0 (lab): internal SDK + server prototype; integration tests with devsandboxes. One-week dogfood.
- Phase 1 (alpha): enable for 5 platform partners (SDK + instrumented) — 4 weeks. Collect telemetry and parse-failure logs.
- Phase 2 (beta): 50 customers, add resume persistence opt-in and mobile SDK low-power mode (buffering thresholds).
- Phase 3 (GA): public docs, migrations guides, sample apps (chat w/ search tool example).

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to self):
- How heavy should in-band schema registry be? embedding schemas increases payload size but avoids round trips. Maybe include only IDs and allow an optional schema prefetch frame at start.
- Resume token format: opaque vs structured? opaque simplifies server evolution but impedes client-side heuristics for partial reassembly.
- How to handle streaming hallucinated action frames (model emits action frame but then contradicts)? Need server-side validation gates before action frames are promoted.
- Billing: per-frame vs per-token semantics. We should keep billing unchanged (per-token) and only expose per-frame telemetry for cost-aware tooling.

Checklist / immediate next steps:
- [ ] Prototype minimal JS SDK with accept/reject action handle (Evan)
- [ ] Server prototype: atomic action emission + resume token (Rhea)
- [ ] Add streaming telemetry hooks in Console (Daniel)
- [ ] Draft spec doc for schema registry and versioning (this doc -> PR)

Appendix: short usage snippet (JS-like pseudo):
const client = new StreamletClient({apiKey});

s.on('progress', (p)=> renderDelta(p.payload));

s.on('action', async (act)=>{
  if(act.type==='search'){
    const handle = s.actionHandle(act.id, act.args);
    // SDK provides typed result deserializer
    const result = await handle.invokeTool({provider:'search-v2'});
    handle.complete();
  }
});

Notes: keep this sketch intentionally lightweight — explicit typed frames should make client code simpler and reduce the need for fragile ad-hoc parsers. This is a draft; will iterate after the lab prototype.
